papers.title: Enabling predictive maintenance in district heating substations: A labelled dataset and fault detection evaluation framework based on service data
papers.what_it_does: PreDist dataset paper (Roelofs, Guevara Bastidas, Hugo, Faulstich, Cadenbach). 93 substations, 2 control-unit manufacturers (M1/M2), 73 faults, 65 pre-defined normal events (30/35). Evaluates EnergyFaultDetector AEs with accuracy on normal events, eventwise F0.5 'reliability' and earliness; criticality threshold chosen by 5-fold stratified CV over the evaluated events (grid 1-100). Full text read (arXiv HTML). Explicitly states: 'the reliability score is overestimated, since we use a balanced dataset ... In reality, the fraction of faults is much lower ... precision is likely lower under realistic class imbalance. Because there is no canonical normal-to-fault ratio, we retain a 50/50 split.'
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Does not quantify the overestimation, does not replay detectors over continuous fleet operation, reports no false alarms per substation-year, no FA-budgeted protocol, no ranking comparison, no cross-manufacturer transfer test (one generic model configuration per manufacturer, trained per event).

papers.title: CARE to Compare: A Real-World Benchmark Dataset for Early Fault Detection in Wind Turbine Data
papers.what_it_does: Gück, Roelofs, Faulstich. 36 turbines, 3 farms, 44 anomaly + 51 normal datasets in the published paper (Zenodo v6 description says 45/50). CARE = weighted average of Coverage (pointwise F_beta, beta=1/2, on anomaly datasets), Accuracy (tn/(fp+tn) on normal datasets, weight 2), Reliability (EVENT-based F_beta, beta=1/2: each dataset is 'alarm' if max criticality >= 72, i.e. ~12 h of consecutive anomalies, compared against dataset labels) and Earliness (weighted score). Full text read (PDF). Paper presents the balanced design as a virtue ('allows for more detailed and meaningful comparison').
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Reliability is NOT a per-year or per-asset false-alarm rate: it is an event-wise F0.5 on a ~50/50 set of hand-selected windows, so it inherits the base-rate inflation. No continuous-deployment replay, no prevalence correction, no statistical power analysis, no cross-farm transfer evaluation (thresholds calibrated per farm). Exact citation: Gück C., Roelofs C.M.A., Faulstich S. Data 2024, 9, 138. Note Zenodo record text cites a different working title ('...A real-world dataset for anomaly detection in wind turbine data').

papers.title: Reproducibility package for 'Detection without discrimination: a blinded, pre-registered test of pre-fault signals in public wind-turbine SCADA data' (Song, manuscript submitted to RESS)
papers.what_it_does: Package opened (README, result JSON, code, manuscript build text). Four-stage pre-registered study on CARE v6, Kelmarsh/Penmanshiel, Fuhrlander: five detectors incl. Fraunhofer energy-fault-detector AE with the official CARE scoring code, random/all-normal/all-anomaly baselines; out-of-sample alarm-budget analysis (threshold fitted on half of normal windows, evaluated on the other half, 10% normal-window alarm budget): 'no alarm raised the odds of a fault by more than about 2'; cross-farm Kelmarsh<->Penmanshiel threshold transfer; random alarm strategy as reference.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Budget is a fraction of normal windows, not false alarms per asset-year; no continuous replay of full operating history; no precision-inflation factor vs balanced benchmark; no district heating/PreDist; no Kendall-tau ranking comparison; no binomial power analysis. Not peer reviewed.

papers.title: Uncertainty-Calibrated Residual Conformal Monitoring of Wind Turbine SCADA Data for Cross-Asset Anomaly Detection Under Distribution Shift
papers.what_it_does: States that calibrating on the same asset/period 'can produce optimistic thresholds, excessive false alarms, and misleading generalization estimates'; nested leave-one-turbine-out asset-disjoint protocol on CARE v6; reports CARE 0.59, alarms in 18/50 normal cases; flags that 36 turbines make estimates exploratory.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Still evaluates on CARE's balanced event windows with CARE score; no per-year FA, no base-rate quantification, no event-vs-continuous ranking comparison, no PreDist, held-out unit is turbine not manufacturer.

papers.title: Chronologically calibrated PCA for wind-turbine SCADA health monitoring: a leakage-controlled CARE v6 benchmark
papers.venue: Wind Energy Science Discussions (preprint under review)
papers.what_it_does: Turbine-disjoint development/locked-test split on CARE v6, chronological threshold calibration on disjoint normal block, cluster-bootstrap CIs; shows paired comparisons between several detectors are not distinguishable; only 5/18 locked-test anomalies detected; false-positive events 17 -> 4.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No continuous deployment replay or per-year FA; no precision-inflation factor; no analytic power for FA rates; no district heating.

papers.title: Low-False-Alarm Evaluation Changes the Ranking of Multisensor Anomaly Detectors
papers.venue: Spectrum - Aplicacoes Operacionais em Areas de Defesa
papers.what_it_does: Shows that evaluating at recall@FAR<=0.05 changes detector rankings vs aggregate metrics in seven model-dataset pairs (MSL, SWaT, water distribution).
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Not energy, FAR is pointwise not per asset-year, no event-window vs continuous protocol, no attribution of the inversion to threshold tuning on evaluated events, no Kendall tau.

papers.title: The Threshold Paradox: Why Calibrating on the Test Set Introduces Bias in Anomaly Detection
papers.what_it_does: Argues that calibrating thresholds on test annotations overestimates performance vs deployment (industrial image AD, MVTec).
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Image AD, not time series/energy; no ranking-inversion measurement; no false alarms per year.

papers.title: Towards a Rigorous Evaluation of Time-Series Anomaly Detection
papers.what_it_does: Point-adjust protocol overestimates performance; random scores become SOTA; comparisons after PA 'can lead to misguided rankings'; untrained model comparable.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: About point adjustment within labelled test series, not about class prior/base rate of balanced event sets or per-year FA; not energy.

papers.title: Current Time Series Anomaly Detection Benchmarks are Flawed and are Creating the Illusion of Progress
papers.what_it_does: Four benchmark flaws incl. 'unrealistic anomaly density'; argues published comparisons unreliable; introduces UCR archive.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Does not quantify deployment precision vs benchmark precision, no FA-per-year, no energy event-window benchmarks.

papers.title: Precision and Recall for Time Series
papers.what_it_does: Range-based precision/recall with tunable existence/overlap/positional bias.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Metric definition only; no base-rate or deployment-rate analysis.

papers.title: Time-Series Aware Precision and Recall for Anomaly Detection (TaPR)
papers.what_it_does: Time-series aware P/R with detection and portion scoring, ambiguous labels.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Metric only; no prevalence/deployment analysis.

papers.title: 'Do you know existing accuracy metrics overrate time-series anomaly detections?' (eTaPR)
papers.what_it_does: Shows existing range metrics overrate imprecise/insufficient detections; proposes eTaPR with cross-referencing and length weighting.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Overrating via metric design, not via class prior of balanced event sets; not energy.

papers.title: Local Evaluation of Time Series Anomaly Detection Algorithms (affiliation metrics)
papers.what_it_does: Adversary can reach high P/R under event metrics; affiliation P/R normalized against a random-sampling baseline.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No per-year FA or base-rate inflation; random baseline is per-event-local, not matched-FA-rate alarms across manufacturers.

papers.title: Navigating the metric maze: a taxonomy of evaluation metrics for anomaly detection in time series
papers.what_it_does: Taxonomy and analysis of 20 TSAD metrics; shows metric choice matters for conclusions.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No deployment base rate, no FA per asset-year, no energy benchmarks.

papers.title: The base-rate fallacy and its implications for the difficulty of intrusion detection
papers.what_it_does: Classic: with low base rate, P(intrusion|alarm) requires unattainably low false-alarm rates; false alarm rate is the limiting factor.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Intrusion detection, analytic; no time-series event-window benchmarks or energy data.

papers.title: The base-rate fallacy and the difficulty of intrusion detection
papers.what_it_does: Journal version of the above.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: As above.

papers.title: Base-Rate Fallacy Redux and a Deep Dive Review in Cybersecurity
papers.what_it_does: Revisits Axelsson; argues false positives dominate; critiques metrics in non-signature IDS.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Cybersecurity only.

papers.title: The Precision-Recall Plot Is More Informative than the ROC Plot When Evaluating Binary Classifiers on Imbalanced Datasets
papers.what_it_does: Precision depends on class ratio; ROC misleading on imbalanced data.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Generic classification; no time series/energy, no event-window design.

papers.title: Classification evaluation (Points of Significance)

papers.what_it_does_not_do: UNVERIFIED content.

papers.title: Development and evaluation of CADe systems in low-prevalence setting: The RARE25 challenge
papers.what_it_does: Prevalence-aware hidden test set; notes strong performance on balanced/enriched sets overestimates clinical utility; PPV low under real prevalence.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Medical imaging; same principle as C1 in a different domain (shows C1 principle is recognised).

papers.title: Anticipation, earliness, alarm cardinality: A new metric for industrial time-series anomaly detection
papers.what_it_does: Industrial TSAD metric (ALARM); shows common metrics give rankings contradicting operator-obvious rankings.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No per-year FA, no base rate, no energy benchmarks.

papers.title: Did We Actually Fix It? An Independent Adversarial Stress-Test of Post-Point-Adjustment Evaluation Metrics
papers.what_it_does: Random detectors vs replacement metrics; best-of-N selection inflates affiliation and ROC metrics; PR metrics floored near prevalence.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Not energy, not event-window balanced sets, not per-year FA.

papers.title: Position: Quo Vadis, Unsupervised Time Series Anomaly Detection?
papers.what_it_does: Flawed metrics/benchmarking; simple baselines competitive with deep SOTA.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No deployment protocol / FA budget; not energy.

papers.title: Towards Unbiased Evaluation of Time-series Anomaly Detector
papers.what_it_does: Balanced point adjustment to counter PA bias.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No base-rate/deployment analysis.

papers.title: Statistical Evaluation of Anomaly Detectors for Sequences
papers.what_it_does: Time-tolerant P/R can overestimate performance; null distributions for significance.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No FA-per-year power analysis; not energy.

papers.title: Anomaly detection in predictive maintenance: A new evaluation framework for temporal unsupervised anomaly detection algorithms
papers.what_it_does: Interval-based positives/negatives; Preceding Window ROC 'preserves the imbalance scheme for evaluation' in PdM.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Does not quantify balanced-vs-continuous precision inflation, no per-year FA, not energy benchmarks.

papers.title: Temporal cross-validation impacts multivariate time series subsequence anomaly detection evaluation
papers.what_it_does: Evaluation design (TSCV) changes AUC-PR and variance.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Not FA-budget/ranking inversion in energy.

papers.title: False Alarm Testing for Radiation Detection Systems
papers.what_it_does: Binomial/Poisson hypothesis tests and power curves for how long/how many observations are needed to verify a false-alarm-rate requirement; links to alarm fatigue.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Radiation portal monitors, not energy fault detection; does not address event-window benchmarks.

papers.title: Statistical Considerations in Designing Tests of Mine Detection Systems: II - Measures Related to the False Alarm Rate
papers.what_it_does: Statistical methods for FAR per unit area/time, sample-size of clutter area, comparing sensors.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Mine detection; same statistics as C4.

papers.title: Benchmark Data and Power Calculations for Evaluating Disease Outbreak Detection Methods
papers.what_it_does: Power-based benchmark design for outbreak detectors.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Surveillance domain.

papers.title: If Nothing Goes Wrong, Is Everything All Right? Interpreting Zero Numerators (rule of three)
papers.what_it_does: Only a Semantic Scholar TLDR retrieved; not counted as opened.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: UNVERIFIED content beyond title.

papers.title: Impact of sample size on false alarm and missed detection rates in PCA-based anomaly detection
papers.what_it_does: FAR dependence on training sample size.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Training-sample effect, not evaluation power.

papers.title: Transfer learning applications for autoencoder-based anomaly detection in wind turbines
papers.what_it_does: Same group as CARE: cross-turbine transfer of AE NBMs; multi-turbine source no better than single; threshold-only fine-tuning can be comparable.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Within-manufacturer turbine transfer with target fine-tuning; no random-alarm matched-FA comparison; no PreDist.

papers.title: Fault detection in new wind turbines with limited data by generative transfer learning
papers.what_it_does: CycleGAN domain mapping across 7 different WTs for NBMs with scarce data.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Positive transfer method; no zero-shot held-out-manufacturer vs random-alarm test.

papers.title: Transfer Learning Approaches for Wind Turbine Fault Detection using Deep Learning
papers.what_it_does: Analyses causes of domain shift between turbines for SCADA fault detection.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No FA-budgeted evaluation or manufacturer hold-out vs random.

papers.title: Farm-Specific Anomaly Detection in Wind Turbine SCADA Data
papers.what_it_does: On CARE farms A/B/C: pooled global model 'cannot hold a stable operating point' (saturates on A, recall 0.19 on C); pointwise all detectors only marginally above trivial all-positive baseline.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No per-year FA, no matched-FA random-alarm baseline, no PreDist, no ranking-inversion analysis.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Validation of an XGBoost Decision Layer for SCADA-Based Wind Turbine Anomaly Detection
papers.what_it_does: Trains on CARE farm A, externally evaluates on unseen farms B and C; 2/3/4-sigma baselines.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Reports positive row-level F1 after transfer; no FA-per-year or random-alarm baseline; supervised.

papers.title: Fleet-Wide Data-Driven Model Generation Process for Residual-Based Fault Detection in Wind Energy
papers.what_it_does: Fleet-wide residual models across farms and manufacturers; notes prior CM limited to a single manufacturer; ROC evaluation.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Positive cross-manufacturer generalization with ROC; no FA per year or base-rate analysis.

papers.title: From lab to practice: Towards a substation-invariant self-supervised transformer for low-label fault detection in district heating
papers.what_it_does: Cross-domain DH experiments: transfer within a network works, asymmetric across networks.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No PreDist cross-manufacturer, no FA budget/random baseline.

papers.title: From bearings to substations: Transfer Learning for fault detection in district heating
papers.what_it_does: Transfer learning from bearing vibration to DH substation dT data; F1 up to 0.91 on operational data.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No continuous-deployment FA evaluation; positive transfer claim.

papers.title: Fault detection for district heating substations: Beyond three-sigma approaches
papers.what_it_does: Shows Gaussian/three-sigma residual assumption fails (seasonality); quantile regression thresholds.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Not about benchmark protocol or ranking; supports that three-sigma is a common DH baseline.

papers.title: No free lunch but a cheaper supper: A general framework for streaming anomaly detection
papers.what_it_does: SAFARI framework; 20 streaming detectors compared; no single best method.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Not fleet-wide DH in abstract (user's description 'fleet-wide' not confirmed by abstract); no FA-per-year.

papers.title: A machine learning approach to fault detection in district heating substations
papers.what_it_does: ML model of one Swedish substation; distinguishes faulty vs well-performing datasets.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Single substation; no FA rate or deployment evaluation.

papers.title: Automated Statistical Methods for Fault Detection in District Heating Customer Installations
papers.what_it_does: Statistical detection of poorly cooling installations among 3000.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No evaluation of FA rates against ground truth.

papers.title: Fault and anomaly detection in district heating substations: A survey on methodology and data sets
papers.what_it_does: Survey; calls for public datasets and industry-relevant metrics as benchmarks.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No metric analysis.

papers.title: Creating a labeled district heating data set: From anomaly detection towards fault detection
papers.what_it_does: Guidelines for DH fault dataset creation.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No evaluation-protocol critique.

papers.title: A Physically Informed Changepoint Score for Fault Prioritisation in District Heating
papers.what_it_does: Reports Average Precision against stated prevalence (0.426) for DH fault ranking.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Prevalence is still enriched case-control; no deployment base-rate correction.

papers.title: Challenges in detection of heating curve misconfiguration: An empirical study
papers.what_it_does: CAE NBM (same group as PreDist) fails on gradual heating-curve faults.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No protocol analysis.

papers.title: scada-fault-bench: an open benchmark for fault detection in wind and PV SCADA data
papers.what_it_does: Benchmark reporting 'false alarm hours per year' with block-bootstrap CIs, plus CARE real faults; simple baselines.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Injected synthetic faults; no balanced-vs-continuous inflation analysis, no DH, no ranking-inversion study; unreviewed.

papers.title: Drift-Aware System Assurance for Wind-Turbine SCADA Condition Monitoring
papers.what_it_does: Forward-in-time evaluation with rolling-threshold persistent alarms; reports operator-facing alarm episodes and healthy alarm hours.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Two fault events; no fleet base-rate or ranking analysis.

papers.title: Anomaly Detection in Wind Turbines: Persistence-Based Alarm Confirmation for False-Alarm Mitigation and Detection-Latency Trade-Offs
papers.what_it_does: Decision-oriented evaluation: alarm persistence rule shapes false alarms vs latency for IF/OCSVM/PCA/AE.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No per-year FA tolerance, no base-rate analysis.

papers.title: An Adaptive Threshold Considering Varying Operation Conditions for Wind Turbine Early Fault Detection and False Alarm Reduction
papers.what_it_does: States false alarms block large-scale deployment; quantifies root causes; 82% FA reduction.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Counts false alarms but no benchmark-protocol critique.

papers.title: The Role Of Reliability Knowledge In Unsupervised Fault Detection Of Wind Turbines
papers.what_it_does: Evaluates OCSVM/IF on open SCADA with false alarm rate, early warning time, alarm persistence.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No protocol comparison.

papers.title: Detecting Changes in Normal Wind Turbine Operations Using Data Driven Approaches
papers.what_it_does: Same AD algorithm behaves differently across NBM choices; no-NBM baseline.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No base-rate/FA-per-year.

papers.title: A Robust Prescriptive Framework and Performance Metric for Diagnosing and Predicting Wind Turbine Faults Based on SCADA and Alarms Data
papers.what_it_does: Argues evaluation 'beyond simple classification metrics' is needed; sliding-window alert metric for real-world deployment.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No base-rate quantification, single farm.

papers.title: Evaluation of Anomaly Detection of an Autoencoder Based on Maintenance Information and SCADA-Data
papers.what_it_does: Fraunhofer AE evaluated against maintenance events: ~35% of failures preceded by many anomalies.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No FA-per-year or protocol comparison.

papers.title: Discussion on the Suitability of SCADA-Based Condition Monitoring for Wind Turbine Fault Diagnosis through Temperature Data Analysis
papers.what_it_does: Controlled 11-year fleet study of 8 turbines; argues SCADA CM suitability usually shown on short, few-turbine analyses.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No FA-budget/base-rate formalism.

papers.title: Deep learning for automated drivetrain fault detection
papers.what_it_does: Fleet-wide performance on 251 bearing failures (vibration).
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Vibration CMS; no event-protocol critique.

papers.title: Economic analysis of condition monitoring systems for offshore wind turbine sub-systems
papers.what_it_does: O&M simulation including CM false alarms and detection rates; costs.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Does not give an operator-tolerable FA/asset-year figure in abstract.

papers.title: Using SCADA data for wind turbine condition monitoring - a review
papers.what_it_does: Review of SCADA CM approaches incl. NBMs.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No FA tolerance number in abstract.

papers.title: Change-point detection in wind turbine SCADA data for robust condition monitoring with normal behaviour models
papers.what_it_does: Change points in 1/3 of signals undermine NBMs (false alarms from training contamination).
papers.what_it_does_not_do: No protocol analysis.

papers.title: Wind Turbine Fault Detection Using Highly Imbalanced Real SCADA Data
papers.what_it_does: Handles imbalanced SCADA data to reduce false positives.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: Training-side imbalance, not evaluation base rate.

papers.title: Moving Generality from Model to Modeler: LLM Agents for PHM on a Deployment-Style Benchmark
papers.what_it_does: Deployment-style benchmark holding out units/conditions; published accuracies rest on own conventions.
papers.what_it_does_not_do: PHM/RUL, not FA-budget event detection.
